name: modus_ponens
description: If P and P implies Q, then Q

name: modus_tollens
description: If not Q and P implies Q, then not P

name: disjunctive_syllogism
description: If P or Q, and not P, then Q

name: conjunction
description: P and Q are both true

name: addition
description: From P, infer P or Q

name: resolution
description: Resolution principle for automated theorem proving

name: proposition
definition: Statement that is either true or false

name: predicate
definition: Function returning truth value

name: quantifier
definition: Specifies quantity of specimens

name: tautology
definition: Formula true under all interpretations

name: contradiction
definition: Formula false under all interpretations

name: contingency
definition: Formula true under some, false under others

name: logical_equivalence
definition: Two formulas with same truth table

name: valid_argument
definition: Impossible for premises true and conclusion false

name: sound_argument
definition: Valid argument with all true premises

name: bayesian_inference
definition: Update probability based on evidence

name: prior_probability
definition: Initial probability before evidence

name: likelihood
definition: Probability of evidence given hypothesis

name: posterior_probability
definition: Updated probability after evidence

name: causal_reasoning
definition: Reasoning about cause-effect relationships

name: do_operator
definition: Intervention: do(X=x) sets X to x

name: counterfactual
definition: What would happen if...
formal: Y_x(u) = value Y would take if X=x in context u

name: confounding
definition: Common cause of treatment and outcome

name: d_separation
definition: Criterion for conditional independence in DAGs

name: backdoor_criterion
definition: Set of variables to adjust for causal effect

name: decision_theory
definition: Framework for optimal choices under uncertainty

name: utility_function
definition: Quantifies preferences over outcomes

name: expected_utility
definition: Σ P(outcome) × Utility(outcome)

name: nash_equilibrium
definition: No player benefits from unilateral deviation

name: pareto_efficiency
definition: No one can be better off without making someone worse off

name: affirming_consequent
why_wrong: Q could be true for other reasons

name: false_dilemma
description: Presenting only two options when more exist

name: post_hoc
description: After this, therefore because of this

name: appeal_to_authority
description: Accepting claim solely because authority says so
